_comment: Model registry for the design-iteration harness.
Contract: every model is invoked non-interactively at MAXIMUM reasoning effort,
receives the brief, and PRINTS a complete HTML document to stdout. The runner
extracts the document and writes it to disk. Models never write files themselves —
that keeps the invocation uniform across three different CLIs.
'available' and the invocation flags are VERIFIED on this machine, not assumed.
PRICING is list API price per 1M tokens, used to cost each session. One design =
one session. Prices move — re-check them before quoting these numbers anywhere
that matters. Sources recorded in design/README.md.

models.label: Claude Opus 5
models.note: claude 2.1.220. --effort max is the ceiling. --output-format json reports usage AND total_cost_usd, which we cross-check against our own computation.

models.label: Claude Fable 5
models.note: Thinking is always on for Fable 5; depth is controlled by effort. Priced above Opus tier — expect this to be the most expensive variant in a round.

models.label: GPT-5.6 Terra
models.note: Mid tier, ~half of Sol. Included specifically to test whether a cheaper tier designs as well against a tightly-specified brief.

models.label: Kimi K3
models.note: kimi -p takes the prompt as its flag VALUE, so -p MUST be last here — the runner appends the prompt after it. --auto is deliberately absent: kimi rejects '--prompt with --auto', and our contract (print HTML to stdout, never write files) needs no tool permissions anyway. Thinking effort is 'high' in ~/.kimi-code/config.toml, its ceiling — there is no per-invocation effort flag, so this one is not literally comparable to the others' max. VERIFIED 2026-07-26: kimi --output-format stream-json emits only role/content messages and a session resume hint — NO token counts. So its cost cannot be computed and is recorded as null, never 0. Estimating from output size would understate it badly, since thinking tokens dominate on a reasoning model and are invisible here.

models.label: OpenCode
models.note: Installed but disabled — it routes across providers, so which model answered would be ambiguous, defeating the comparison. Flip to true and pin a provider to include it.
